text: Given a behavioural property, a tool can be at most two of: sound, terminating, and ___ .
explanation: Java's definite-assignment analysis keeps soundness and termination and therefore rejects some correct programs — which is why `int x; if (alwaysTrue()) x = 1; use(x);` does not compile. Type systems make the same trade: they decide "no type errors", which is weaker than "no errors" and is checkable. Every real tool is conservative, accepts false positives, accepts false negatives, or bounds its effort.
